description.text: Night presses close beyond a rain-covered bus window, and the glass fills most of the frame. Condensation softens the surface into a milky veil, broken by scattered beads of water that catch muted amber and pale white glints from city lights. Those lights remain far beyond the pane, dissolving into soft halos and long, wavering smears rather than readable signs or buildings. The dark interior edge of the window frames the view at the top and side, making the glass feel like a glowing plane suspended in shadow. Droplets tremble in place, gather weight, and begin to run in crooked trails, clearing thin channels through the mist. Each moving bead drags a small distorted highlight with it, and the light beyond bows and stretches inside the water. Nearby beads stay pinned to the glass, so the first trails stand out as slow, irregular lines. The surface looks cool and slick, with the rain's gradual movement providing the only visible change.
Rain beads across the window while blurred amber and white city lights glow beyond the glass.
Droplets gather and begin to slide in uneven trails, opening thin clear paths through the condensation.
Rain taps softly against the glass, underlaid by a low bus engine hum.
The camera holds a static shot.

The shot cuts to a tighter view of the same rain-covered bus window. A single large droplet sits near the center of the glass, surrounded by a scatter of smaller beads and a fine web of condensation. Beyond the pane, nighttime city lights remain out of focus, their amber and white glows smeared into soft bands by the wet surface. The large droplet trembles, draws a smaller neighbor into its edge, and swells until its outline stretches. It then breaks downward into a quick rivulet, cutting a wavering path through the mist. Inside that moving trail, the blurred lights warp, narrow, and slide, briefly sharpening into a bright thread before softening again. The surrounding beads stay pinned in place, making the rivulet's travel stand out against the otherwise still glass. The window's cool, slick surface and the dark interior frame remain constant around the shifting water, with the wider view reduced to soft shapes and reflected glints.
The tighter view isolates a large droplet surrounded by smaller beads on the misted glass.
The large droplet merges with a smaller one, swells, and breaks into a quick rivulet that warps the passing light.
A faint hiss of tires on wet asphalt rises beyond the glass.
The camera holds a static shot.
